mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through improved economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS increasing by at least 50k compared to prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals robust aggregate demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through stronger economic expansion.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS increase by at least 1% month-over-month, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, high industrial production (INDPRO) indicates economic overheating and impending monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through profit margin compression.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, INDPRO levels above 110 (index 2017=100) are associated with positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.5% signals strong housing market activity that boosts construction sector earnings and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When HOUST increases by more than 1.5% month-over-month, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through improved corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through reduced economic growth expectations.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% month-over-month, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.
